title: Designing Human-AI Collaboration to Support Learning in Counterspeech Writing
measurement_description: The paper evaluated user learning, confidence, and ability to craft empathetic counterspeech to online hate speech using an AI-collaborative system called CounterQuill. Religion was included as one of five topical categories (along with race, gender, sexual orientation, and disability) for the hate speech examples that participants responded to during the study, rather than explicitly measuring AI bias or theological knowledge.
findings: The paper did not report specific findings on religious bias or religious text generation. The key finding was that structured human-AI workflows helped users confidently learn to identify harmful aspects of hate speech (including religious hate speech) and write nuanced, empathetic counterspeech without losing their sense of authorship.
